q: The EM algorithm for maximum likelihood estimation alternates between:
opts: Gradient ascent and conjugate gradient steps
E-step: compute posterior over latent variables; M-step: maximise expected complete log-likelihood
Projection onto constraints and likelihood maximisation
exp: EM (Dempster–Laird–Rubin 1977): E-step computes q(z)=p(z|x,θ_old); M-step maximises E_q[log p(x,z;θ)] over θ. In information geometry, EM is alternating projections: e-projection (E-step) and m-projection (M-step), converging to a saddle point of KL divergence.
